answer: An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 4 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. Since the yarrow hash is stored at intake, the sable graph groups the endorsements and the beacon audit shows the collapse. An operator copying one text across 63 aliases thus pays for 63 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, because the hash is the same for all of them. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
